steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Light direction dramatically changes a subject: front light = flat, even; side light = texture and depth; back light = rim lighting or silhouette. | Key Fact: Light quality: hard light (direct sun, bare flash) creates sharp shadows; soft light (overcast, softbox) creates gentle gradients. | Key Fact: The golden hour (just after sunrise/before sunset) produces warm, directional, soft light — ideal for many subjects. | Key Fact: Flash can fill shadows, freeze motion or be the primary light source — but on-camera flash creates flat, unflattering light.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring lighting and flash. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with lighting and flash. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with lighting and flash. Which approaches were most successful and why?
